critical_code_review_comments: Non-blocking (carried from iter_9): DocEditorCore <option> children still emit the injected <span data-ve-dynamic> wrapper causing 'span cannot be a child of option' React hydration warning. Preview-instrumentation issue, doesn't affect functionality.

Non-blocking: SheetEditorCore chart panel closes on grid click via the outer div's onClick={setChartOpen(false)}, which is good; consider also closing on Escape for keyboard a11y (docs popovers had the same minor gap).

Non-blocking: SheetEditorCore.sortCol() re-writes only the numeric entries in the selected column (skipping formulas/text) — this is correct for the m7 task but could be surprising if the header cell were numeric. Not a bug for current curriculum.
Non-blocking observation: /studio/{track_id} generic route returns 404 for unknown tracks correctly; no route-ordering issue between sheets and docs.
Optional: consider a Pydantic schema for MissionSubmit doc payload (defense-in-depth); currently accepts any dict.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Skill Studio Docs (Phase 1) + Sheets (Phase 2) are both green. Backend suite: /app/backend/tests/test_skillstudio.py (docs, 25 cases) + /app/backend/tests/test_skillstudio_sheets.py (sheets, 25 cases). Both classes are loadscope-pinned via xdist for deterministic ordering. _perfect_doc() in the sheets test applies cell_value tasks BEFORE cell_formula so shared-cell tasks (e.g. m2 t1=formula & t2=value) don't overwrite each other — reuse this pattern for future sheets missions. If Slides track (Phase 3) lands, mirror the same TestSkillStudioSheets structure. Frontend cookie injection continues to work on the preview host. The React 'span in option' hydration warning is preview-tooling injected, not product code.
rca of the issue: None — no bugs found. Phase 2 Sheets shipped clean. Initial pytest run showed 7 assertion failures caused by my _perfect_doc() applying cell_formula THEN cell_value, which overwrites the formula string with a plain number and fails the cell_formula check; fix was to reverse the order (values first, formulas last) since the formula evaluates to the same number, satisfying both check kinds simultaneously — this is a TEST-only fix, not a product fix.
